newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Seats in Nicaraguan parliament sorted out.
newsitem.headline: Seats in Nicaraguan parliament sorted out.

text.p: Nicaraguan President-elect Arnoldo Aleman's right-wing Liberal Alliance will control 42 of the 93 seats in the National Assembly, coming up short of an outright majority, according to final results announced on Wednesday.

The left-wing Sandinista Front will hold 36 seats, Rosa Marina Zelaya, president of the Supreme Electoral Council, told a news conference in announcing the final distribution of seats resulting from the Oct. 20 elections.
The evangelical Christian Road Party won four seats, and eight parties will share the remaining 11 seats.
The National Assembly is nearly equal to the presidency in power and has wide authority over the budget, political appointments and foreign treaties.

Final election results were delayed until now because several political parties had complained about the council's interpretation of the election law in determining the distribution of seats, and had demanded a revision.
The revision, however, led to no major changes.
Aleman and the new assembly will take over on Jan. 10.
